transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me today, I really appreciate it. Um, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I came in because... well, I guess I've just been worrying a lot lately. Probably more than I should be. 

It's just everyday things, really. I'm a real estate broker, so I worry about my clients, the market, money, my family... even little things like whether moving into my new condo was the right decision. I know it's probably silly, and I try not to let it bother anyone, but the worrying just feels a little... out of proportion to what's actually happening? 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right for you.
Do you find that your worrying is especially focused on situations where you're around other people, like meetings or social gatherings?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. Um, I'm actually pretty okay in social situations. With my job, you know, I'm constantly talking to clients, running open houses, or going to meetings, and I really do enjoy that part of it. I don't want to give you the wrong impression—I can definitely still do my job and be around people just fine. 

It's not the people themselves that make me nervous. It's more just... the background worries about everything else, usually when I have a quiet moment to overthink. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is that what you were asking?
Do you find that you worry on most days, even when there isn't a specific event or problem happening?

Um, well... I'm not really sure if it's most days. I haven't really kept track of it like that. And I don't think it happens when there's absolutely *nothing* going on. 

Usually, my mind just latches onto something real, like a pending sale or, you know, getting things set up at the condo. I try really hard to focus on the positive, so I wouldn't say I'm just sitting around worrying for no reason at all. There's almost always some little prompt for it, even if I blow it a bit out of proportion. 

I hope that's the kind of information you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm answering you correctly and not making it sound worse than it actually is.
Have you noticed any physical symptoms, like feeling restless, having trouble relaxing, or muscle tension, when you're worrying?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I don't want to make it sound like I'm falling apart or anything, because I'm really not. But, um, I suppose by the end of the day, I do notice my neck and shoulders feeling a bit... tight? Almost like I've been bracing myself without realizing it. 

And, well, sometimes when I'm driving between listings or just sitting at my desk, I'll catch myself clenching my jaw. It's probably just normal stress from the job, right? I mean, everyone gets a little tense sometimes. I try to stretch it out so it doesn't bother anyone. 

Does that sound like what you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right details without, you know, overstating things.
Have you noticed feeling unusually tired or fatigued, even if you haven't been doing anything particularly strenuous?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I have a pretty busy schedule, so if I'm tired, it's usually because I've actually been running around doing things. I don't really just sit around feeling exhausted for no reason. 

I try to make sure I get enough sleep so I can be on my game for work, you know? I wouldn't want my clients to think I'm dragging. So, um, no, I wouldn't say I feel unusually fatigued. Just the normal amount of tired at the end of a long day. Is that... does that answer your question? I hope I'm not being too vague.
Do you find it hard to control or stop the worrying, even when you try to distract yourself or focus on something else?

Um, I wouldn't say it's completely out of my control, because I really do try my best to manage it. But, well... sometimes, even when I tell myself, "Parin, this is not urgent," it can be a little tricky to just switch it off. It's like one little concern sort of naturally leads to another? And then, before I even realize it, I might have spent, I don't know, maybe half an hour just replaying small details in my head that I really meant to let go of. 

I always manage to pull myself together, though! I hope that doesn't make me sound, um, obsessive or anything. I just want to do right by my clients and make sure everything is perfect for them. Is that... does that make sense for what you're asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture without making it sound worse than it is.
Do you find that you feel anxious or worried on more days than not, even if it’s just a background sense of unease?

Oh, um... no, I definitely wouldn't say it's more days than not. I really try to keep a positive outlook, you know? In my line of work, you kind of have to project confidence for your clients, so I make sure I have plenty of good days. 

If I have a worry, it's usually just tied to a specific closing or a tricky inspection, not just... sitting there in the background all week for no reason. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm walking around a nervous wreck all the time, because I'm really not! Most days are perfectly fine and productive. 

I hope that's the kind of information you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture.
Have you noticed yourself becoming more irritable or easily annoyed lately, even by small things that wouldn’t usually bother you?

Um, irritable? Oh, gosh, no. I really pride myself on being patient, especially with my clients. You know, buying a house is stressful for people, so I have to be the calm one. 

I mean, sure, if someone doesn't send over a document when they said they would, I might get a tiny bit frustrated, but that's just normal professional standards, right? I certainly don't snap at people or get annoyed over silly little things. I always try to keep a smile on and keep things moving smoothly. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too... demanding about my work? I just like things done right, but I'm definitely not an irritable person. Does that answer what you were asking?
Have you noticed any trouble focusing or keeping your attention on tasks, like reading through contracts or following conversations, because your mind is preoccupied with worries?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I have trouble focusing in a big way. I mean, I'm very detail-oriented, which you have to be in real estate! But, I suppose... occasionally, if I'm reviewing something really dense, like a purchase agreement or an inspection addendum, I might... well, I might find myself reading the same paragraph three or four times? 

It's just that sometimes a little thought about a different client or a deadline might pop into my head, and I just sort of lose the thread of what I was checking for a second. But I always catch it right away and refocus! I just want to make sure I don't miss a single detail for my buyers. 

I hope that doesn't make it sound like I'm not paying attention to my work? I'm actually very thorough. Is that... is that the kind of thing you meant?
Have you ever noticed symptoms like your heart racing, sweating, or shaking when you're feeling particularly worried or anxious?

Oh, goodness, no... nothing like that. I definitely don't get shaky or start sweating. I mean, can you imagine if I was sitting at a closing table with a buyer and just started sweating or shaking? My clients would be absolutely horrified! No, I always make sure to present a very calm, put-together image. 

My heart might beat a tiny bit faster if I'm, say, stuck in traffic and running late for a showing, but that's just normal rushing around, right? It's definitely not from just sitting and worrying. I really pride myself on keeping my composure, so I don't have those kinds of extreme physical reactions. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have those things to report? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers and not leaving out anything you need.
Has your worrying ever made it difficult for you to function normally in your job, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Oh, "difficult to function" sounds so... severe. I definitely wouldn't use those words. I'm still very dedicated to my work! But, um... I suppose, if I'm being completely open with you—and I do want to make sure I'm answering you properly—I have noticed that some things at work are taking me a bit longer than they used to. 

Just... straightforward things, really, like standard listing negotiations or reviewing contracts. And, well, I guess I have had to delay returning a few client calls lately. Not because I'm not doing my job! It's just that I... I don't always feel confident I've checked every single detail carefully enough yet, and I want to be absolutely sure before I talk to them. 

That just means I'm being extra conscientious, right? I really hope that doesn't make me sound incompetent. I just want everything to be perfect for my buyers and sellers. Does that make sense, or is that the sort of thing you were looking for?
Do you find that your anxiety or worry tends to persist even after the specific problem or stressor has been resolved, or does it usually go away once the situation is taken care of?

Oh, I think it usually goes away! Yes, definitely. Once a closing is finalized and the keys are handed over, I'm just so thrilled for my clients. I don't keep worrying about that specific house, you know? 

I mean, I suppose... sometimes, I might double-check my files a day or two later just to make absolutely certain the escrow company got all the final addendums, even though I know it's done. But that's just being thorough, isn't it? It's not that I'm still anxious about it, I just like to tie up loose ends neatly. 

Once a problem is solved, I'm very good at moving on to the next client. I really don't let things linger and drag me down. I hope that's the right way to handle it? I just try to stay as professional and forward-focused as possible.
Do you ever feel anxious or on edge about things that might happen in the future, even when there's no specific event or problem that you're currently dealing with?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say I just sit around feeling anxious about nothing. That sounds like I have too much time on my hands! I always like to stay productive. 

I mean, I suppose I do think ahead a lot. In real estate, you sort of have to, right? You're always anticipating what the market might do next quarter, or worrying—well, not worrying, just *planning*—for whether interest rates are going to fluctuate. But I don't just feel on edge out of the blue. There's always a practical reason for me to be thinking about the future. 

I really try to stay positive and focused on what I can control. I wouldn't want you to think I'm just borrowing trouble or being pessimistic. That's just being a responsible professional, don't you think? I hope that answers your question properly!
Would you say that you experience worry or anxiety on more days than not, even if it’s just a mild feeling in the background?

Oh, more days than not? No, I really don't think so. I mean, I have wonderful days! Most days I'm just busy and, well, engaged with my clients. I certainly wouldn't want to paint a picture of myself as someone who is constantly fretting all week long. 

I suppose... well, maybe there is sometimes a little, um, hum of energy in the background? But I always just thought of that as my professional drive, you know? Keeping me on my toes so I don't miss any important details for my buyers. I wouldn't call it anxiety, really. It's just being alert and ready for the day. 

I try very hard to keep a positive attitude, and I think I do a pretty good job of it. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you an accurate picture without making myself sound, well, worse than I am. Am I explaining that okay?
Do you ever feel worried or anxious even when everything in your life feels stable and there are no clear problems to solve?

Well... I suppose... I mean, I know I just said I try to stay so positive, and I really do! But... oh, I guess if I'm being completely honest, that is actually why I made the appointment to see you today. I just didn't want to make a bad impression right off the bat or sound like I can't handle my own life. 

But lately, even when things are perfectly fine, I just seem to worry about, well, everything. My clients, the market, my family, money... I even fret over whether moving to the condo was the right decision, which is already done and over with! It just... it feels a little out of proportion to what is actually happening in my life right now. 

I don't want to sound like a neurotic person, because I really am very capable, you know? I just want to make sure I'm managing things correctly. Do you think it's normal to get a little overwhelmed like that sometimes?
Do you find that you still feel anxious or worried even when there are no real problems or stressors in your life at that moment?

Oh, um... I think that's sort of what I was just trying to say a moment ago? I hope I didn't confuse things! But yes, like I mentioned, even when there aren't any actual problems right in front of me, my mind just sort of keeps going over things—like the condo, or my clients. 

I don't really have anything else to add to that, really. It's just that same feeling I was just describing. I'm sorry, I don't want to sound like a broken record! Am I giving you the right kind of information? I just want to be as helpful as possible without sounding like I'm sitting here complaining about a wonderful life.
Do you find that your anxiety or worry comes up even when there are no specific things in your life at that moment to be anxious about?

Oh, dear. I feel like we're going in circles, and I'm so sorry if I'm not being clear enough! I really don't mean to be difficult. 

Yes, it's just like I was saying before... even when there's absolutely nothing wrong, my mind still finds something to fret about. I hope that makes sense? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly. I don't want you to think I'm not listening!
Do you ever feel anxious or worried even when you’re not thinking about specific things like work, your family, or the condo?

Oh, I see! I'm so sorry, I think I finally understand what you're asking now. I really didn't mean to make this so difficult for you! 

Um... well, it's hard to say, because my mind just always seems to find its way back to those exact things. Like I mentioned when we first started talking, that's really the whole reason I made the appointment today. Even if I'm just sitting quietly, not trying to think about anything at all, suddenly I'm worrying about the market, or money, or my family... it just sort of takes over and fills in the blanks, if that makes sense? 

And like I said, it just feels so out of proportion to my actual reality right now, since everything is generally fine. I know I keep listing the same worries, and I'm so sorry for repeating myself! I just want to be sure I'm giving you a clear picture of what goes on in my head. Is that a bit closer to what you were asking?
